title: Use prebuilt planner binaries in CI
description:
Avoid rebuilding cargo-affect in every CI run just to compute the affected package set.

## Files
- action.yml
- scripts/install.sh
- README.md
- release workflow, later if needed

## Approach
Action install should prefer a pinned release binary, then a restored tool cache, and only fall back to cargo install for local development or unreleased SHAs. Keep this backend-neutral so WarpBuild, GitHub-hosted, and Blacksmith all benefit.

## Plan Reference
- planning/cargo-affect/02-github-action-ci-backends.md (Install behavior)
close_reason: Added install script and release workflow so CI can use prebuilt binaries or a tool cache before source fallback.

title: Cargo Affect
description:
Build a reusable Cargo subcommand for planning affected Rust workspace validation from git changes.

## Success Criteria
- Changed packages plus reverse workspace dependents are selected from cargo metadata.
- Outputs support Cargo args, nextest expressions, JSON plans, and explanations.
- Unknown or global changes fail open by selecting all packages.
- CI integration stays backend-neutral, with WarpBuild as the first recipe and GitHub-hosted/Blacksmith support planned.
